title: Learning and Forecasting Multiscale Spatiotemporal Epidemic Dynamics with Lagrangian-Eulerian Graph Neural ODEs
abstract: arXiv:2610.21223v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate medium- to long-range epidemic forecasting requires extrapolating high-dimensional, heterogeneous and nonstationary dynamics from partial observations. Yet hybrid models often leave implicit which observations inform which epidemic processes and how learned graph interactions modify system state. We introduce LE-EpiGNODE, which replaces generic message passing with process-specific, mechanism-guided neural operators: age-contact information drives Lagrangian infection generation, whereas mobility drives conservative Eulerian population transport within a structure-preserving universal differential equation. We evaluated LE-EpiGNODE across 14 controlled synthetic mechanisms spanning time-modulated, state-dependent, nonlinear and coupled dynamics, three complementary COVID-19 settings, 21 comparator models and five targeted ablations. tldr: 提出LE-EpiGNODE模型，以机制引导的拉格朗日-欧拉图神经常微分方程取代通用消息传递，将年龄-接触信息用于感染生成、人口流动用于保守性人口运输，在中长期流行病时空预测中取得显著优势。
en_tdlr: LE-EpiGNODE replaces generic message passing with mechanism-guided Lagrangian-Eulerian graph neural ODEs—mapping age-contact data to infection generation and mobility to conservative population transport—achieving increasingly pronounced forecasting gains at longer epidemic prediction horizons.
